intent_and_evidence: Personalized workout plans need different exercise sets per fitness goal. Each goal is a separate class implementing base_exercises(); recommend() adjusts sets for difficulty. recommend_workout selects one strategy at runtime from the requested goal or the goal inferred from Member.fitness_goals (infer_goal_from_text, workout_recommendation.py:120-136; reused by SpecializationMatchPolicy in Change2) and calls strategy.recommend(difficulty) without knowing the concrete class. Adding a goal means adding a class, not editing conditionals.

intent_and_evidence: Trainer-assignment rules vary (match goals to specialization, balance load, prefer rating). Each rule is a class implementing select_trainer(member, candidates, loads). assign_trainer applies the shared eligibility rules (active trainer, under max_clients) and then delegates the choice to the selected policy (trainer_assignment.py:127-128) without knowing which one it is. The admin picks the policy per assignment or for auto-assign.

participant_roles: Subject=AttendancePublisher (subscribe, unsubscribe, notify); Observer=AttendanceObserver (abstract update); ConcreteObservers=InAppNotificationObserver, EmailNotificationObserver, SmsNotificationObserver, TrainerAlertObserver; Event=AttendanceEvent (attendance_marked, class_missed, streak_milestone); Publishers=scan_qr, mark_manual_attendance and close_class routes
intent_and_evidence: Attendance actions must notify several parties without the attendance routes knowing who they are. The routes only publish an AttendanceEvent to attendance_publisher; each subscribed observer reacts independently: an in-app notification, an email or SMS that respects the member's attendance_alerts and sms_opt_in preferences, and an alert to the member's assigned trainer (from Change2) for missed classes and streak milestones. AttendancePublisher.notify loops over the subscribed observers and calls update(event, db, background_tasks). Adding a new channel means writing one observer and subscribing it, without editing attendance.py.
change_description: Introduced in Change3 for attendance notifications: check-ins, streak milestones (3/7/14/30 days) and no-shows (recorded by the new close-class endpoint) are broadcast to decoupled notification observers.

participant_roles: Subject=NotificationsService unreadCountSubject and latestSubject (BehaviorSubject), exposed as unreadCount$ and latest$; Observers=AppComponent template async-pipe subscriptions (badge and notification panel); Producer=startPolling, refresh, markRead and markAllRead; additional Subject=AuthService.currentUser$, observed by AppComponent to start or stop polling
intent_and_evidence: The alerts badge and panel must update whenever the unread count changes, whether from polling or from the user marking notifications read. NotificationsService keeps the state in BehaviorSubjects and pushes new values with next(); AppComponent's template subscribes through the async pipe, so the view is notified instead of asking for data. AppComponent also subscribes to AuthService.currentUser$ to start polling on login and stop it on logout.
change_description: Introduced in Change3: the frontend alerts bell observes notification state published by the shared NotificationsService, so in-app attendance notifications appear without a page reload.
